title: Impact of SULT1A3/SULT1A4 genetic polymorphisms on the sulfation of phenylephrine and salbutamol by human SULT1A3 allozymes
authors: Bairam AF, Rasool MI, Alherz FA, Abunnaja MS, El Daibani AA, Gohal SA, et al.
funder: This work was supported in part by a grant from National Institutes of Health (Grant # R03HD071146).
authorConflicts: The authors declare no conflicts of interest.
result: Twelve purified SULT1A3 allozymes, expressed from SULT1A3 and SULT1A4 single-nucleotide polymorphisms, sulfated salbutamol at rates differing from the wild-type enzyme. With 50 µM salbutamol, SULT1A3-S8P and -N235T showed 16.3% and 22.5% of wild-type specific activity, SULT1A3-P101H and -R144C were comparable to wild type, and seven others showed 50 to 75%. Michaelis constants and maximum rates differed as well, as they did with phenylephrine.
